directAnswer: To repair Windows Update, you can run the Windows Update Troubleshooter and reset the Windows Update components manually if necessary.
summary: This guide provides steps to troubleshoot and repair issues with Windows Update, ensuring your system stays up to date.

sections.heading: Using the Windows Update Troubleshooter
sections.body: The Windows Update Troubleshooter can automatically detect and fix common issues with Windows Update. It's a good first step in resolving update problems.

sections.heading: Resetting Windows Update Components
sections.body: If the troubleshooter doesn't resolve the issue, you may need to manually reset the Windows Update components using Command Prompt.

steps.title: Run the Windows Update Troubleshooter
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters > Windows Update. Click 'Run the troubleshooter' and follow the prompts.

steps.title: Reset Windows Update Components
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as an administrator and run the following commands one by one: 'net stop wuauserv', 'net stop cryptSvc', 'net stop bits', 'net stop msiserver', then 'net start wuauserv', 'net start cryptSvc', 'net start bits', 'net start msiserver'.

faqs.question: What if the troubleshooter doesn't fix the issue?
faqs.answer: If the troubleshooter fails to resolve the problem, consider resetting the Windows Update components manually as described in the steps above.

faqs.question: How do I check for updates after repairing?
faqs.answer: After completing the repair steps, go to Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update and click 'Check for updates' to see if updates are available.

faqs.question: Will this affect my installed programs?
faqs.answer: Repairing Windows Update should not affect your installed programs, but it's always a good idea to back up important data before making system changes.

caveats: Some steps may vary depending on your version of Windows 10 or 11.
